body:
```
/*
 * Copyright (c) 1987 Regents of the University of California.
 * All rights reserved.
 *
 * Redistribution and use in source and binary forms are permitted
 * provided that this notice is preserved and that due credit is given
 * to the University of California at Berkeley. The name of the University
 * may not be used to endorse or promote products derived from this
 * software without specific written prior permission. This software
 * is provided ``as is'' without express or implied warranty.
 */
```

This license was quite common. A recursive grep of the TUHS archive shows 785 instances of the phrase `provided that this notice is preserved and due credit is given`.

It is the license on many files in 2.10.1BSD, 2.11BSD, 4.3BSD-Reno and a lot of usenet postings for networking software for 4.3BSD or other platforms in the sources USENET groups. The net-2 sources have moved to what looks like a BSD-4-clause license. The 4.3BSD code is marked with variation. So this license appears to fill the gap between 4.3BSD and 4.3BSD-Reno. 2.10BSD and 4.3BSD-Tahoe also appear to have 4.3BSD markings. Some of the sources posted to the USENET sources use it and claim to be for 4.3BSD-Tahoe... This series of releases suggests that it started late 1988 and apart from 2.11BSD retaining it, abandoned by 1991 for Net-2. Net-1 used something else...

4.3BSD and earlier had markings like:
```
 * Copyright (c) 1982, 1986 Regents of the University of California.
 * All rights reserved.  The Berkeley software License Agreement
 * specifies the terms and conditions for redistribution.
```
Net-1 has something strangely more complex:
```
 * Copyright (c) 1980, 1986 Regents of the University of California.
 * All rights reserved.
 *
 * Redistribution and use in source and binary forms are permitted
 * provided that the above copyright notice and this paragraph are
 * duplicated in all such forms and that any documentation,
 * advertising materials, and other materials related to such
 * distribution and use acknowledge that the software was developed
 * by the University of California, Berkeley.  The name of the
 * University may not be used to endorse or promote products derived
 * from this software without specific prior written permission.
 * THIS SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED ``AS IS'' AND WITHOUT ANY EXPRESS OR
 * IMPLIED WARRANTIES, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED
 * WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTIBILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
```
I've not done an extensive analysis of all these instances to hunt for variation. I expect there'd
be little to none in the BSD releases at least: This text was inserted by SCCS before the release
from a template. The USENET postings appear to be verbatim copies from the BSD released files.
And there's only about a dozen of them. Only 1 is original work, and the license appears there
to document the original license for the file which was rewritten.
Based on the above, I'd suggest the name `BSD-4.3RENO` based on the first use, or `2.11BSD` based on the largest user today (latest release Sept 1, 2022), with a small preference for the latter.

I've changed the suggested short identifier to BSD-4.3RENO because of my slight preference for referencing the earliest known use but I don't have any strong objection to @bsdimp's preferred alternative of 2.11BSD.
2.11BSD has a mix of 4.3BSD, 4.3BSD-RENO and other licenses too (since it's best viewed as an early distribution), so I'm good either way.

Coincidentally, someone asked on twitter, and so I did this thread which adds a little to the color here. https://twitter.com/bsdimp/status/1572521676268802049
The license doesn't appear to be the overall license in BSD4.3-Reno, but does appear extensively there. And many files use this variation as well
```
/*-
 * Copyright (c) 1990 The Regents of the University of California.
 * All rights reserved.
 *
 * This code is derived from software contributed to Berkeley by
 * Ed James.
 *
 * Redistribution and use in source and binary forms are permitted
 * provided that: (1) source distributions retain this entire copyright
 * notice and comment, and (2) distributions including binaries display
 * the following acknowledgement:  ``This product includes software
 * developed by the University of California, Berkeley and its contributors''
 * in the documentation or other materials provided with the distribution
 * and in all advertising materials mentioning features or use of this
 * software. Neither the name of the University nor the names of its
 * contributors may be used to endorse or promote products derived
 * from this software without specific prior written permission.
 * THIS SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED ``AS IS'' AND WITHOUT ANY EXPRESS OR
 * IMPLIED WARRANTIES, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED
 * WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
 */
```
So there might be more variation than I allowed earlier...  So you should only read this as evidence supporting use in several places (so not unique) rather than a complete treatment of all variations.

## Definitive Factors


1. **Is the submitted license unique, that is, it does not match another license already on the License List as per the [matching guidelines](https://spdx.org/spdx-license-list/matching-guidelines)?**
    - [X] Yes => the phrase "and that due credit is given" doesn't appear to be included in any existing list on the list

    - [X] Yes

    - [X] Yes
    - [ ] No
1. **Has the license steward, if any, committed to versioning new versions and to not modify it after addition to the list?**
    - [ ] Yes
    - [ ] No
    - => historical license, not really applicable here

## Other factors for inclusion

*Roughly in order of descending importance*

1. **Does the license substantially comply with one of the free/open content definitions? (examples include the [Open Source Definition](https://opensource.org/osd) and the [Debian Free Software Guidelines](https://www.debian.org/social_contract#guidelines))** (_Approval by the organisation that publishes the definition is not required_)
    - [X] Yes => simple attribution-style permissive license
    - [ ] No
1. **Is the license structured to be generally usable by anyone, and not specific to one organisation or project?**
    - [ ] Yes
    - [X] No => specific to UC Berkeley, but could be templated as with other BSD-style licenses
1. **Does the license have substantial use such that it is likely to be encountered (ie. use in many projects, or in one significant project)?** (_For recently written licenses, definitive plans for it to be used in at least one or a few significant projects may satisfy this_)
    - [X] Yes => see comments above re: historical BSD versions, GNU utils
    - [ ] No
1. **Is the license primarily intended to facilitate the free distribution of content with limited restrictions?**
    - [X] Yes
    - [ ] No
1. **Does the license steward support this submission, or is at least aware of and not in opposition of it?**
    - [ ] Yes
    - [X] No => not aware of steward involvement here

+1 to add, meets FOSS requirements and widely used in BSD / GNU / etc.
